correctness.rationale: For all prime powers q, the Solomon–Tits building is simply connected; all elements of the 1+3 block group fix the distinguished line, and Armstrong gives trivial quotient pi_1. The three fixed-poset types and their counts are exhaustive because degree-three field extension is prime and nontrivial base scalars act semisimply. The multiplicative subspace-lattice Möbius function gives fixed Euler values 1+q^6, 1+q^3, 2, and the exact identity (q^6+q^4-q-1)/(q^3-1)=q^3+q+1. The dimension-two quotient then has free H_2 of rank q^3+q and is a wedge of that many spheres by Hurewicz and Whitehead. Binary 65,315,315-to-11,45,45 orbit counts, exact boundary identities, Smith units and the polynomial test were independently reproduced from verify.py; finite q cases are checks, not universal proof.

originality.rationale: Actual cross-object comparisons distinguish the new reducible, globally point-fixing Singer block from all previously published irreducible projective Singer-group and normalizer actions. The claim is neither a parameter substitution nor an immediate instance of those published quotient formulas. Full relevant published results and primary building/flat-orbit source material were inspected to the extents recorded; remaining unindexed-priority and general Steinberg-character implication risks are disclosed.
residual_risks: Unindexed or unpublished sources may have given the same fixed-line cyclic building quotient or used parabolic Steinberg character restrictions to deduce its sphere number.

Only introductory excerpts of Armstrong and selected pages of Drudge and Arone–Dwyer were directly inspected; their main hypotheses distinguish their subjects, but source-exhaustive negative claims are avoided.

value.rationale: The result classifies a canonical infinite family of ordinary rank-four spherical-building quotients attached to a maximal Singer block in a parabolic Levi factor, uniformly for all prime powers q, with an exact nontrivial rank q^3+q. The contrast with the irreducible Singer quotient (which has cyclic first-homology torsion) is structurally meaningful. It resolves the full integral homotopy type rather than a single count or a routine normalization check, and the explicit rank is relevant for comparing finite-field spherical links and isotropy actions.
